Determine a set of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ that generate the parabola shown above. Express your answer in the form $x=p{t}^{2},y=2pt,$ where $p$ is a constant.

$x=$
{{field-1}},
$\,y=$
{{field-2}}
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(-5,-4).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=p{t}^{2},\,y=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(-5,-4),$ we can substitute $x=-5$ and $y=-4$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}-5=p{t}^{2} \\ -4=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =2pt \\ t & =-\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-5 & =p{(-\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ -5 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ p & =-\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=(-\frac{4}{5}){t}^{2},\,y=2(-\frac{4}{5})t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=-\frac{4}{5}{t}^{2},\,y=-\frac{8}{5}t.
$$
